**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in ALAS2 in patients with X-linked erythropoietic protoporphyria, or the lack of impact of COX15 dysfunction on heme biosynthesis in patients with congenital sideroblastic anemia, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of a common benign variant in ALAS2 in the general population (e.g., >1% allele frequency in gnomAD) would weaken the claim of ALAS2 as a primary driver for X-linked EPP if it were not for the specific context of X-linked inheritance and established causality.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared involvement of the heme biosynthesis pathway in both X-linked erythropoietic protoporphyria and COX15-deficient congenital sideroblastic anemia could pave the way for targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating heme production or iron metabolism, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
